Using the Beige Book lens, the FOMC’s aggressive March 15, 2020 easing (policy rate to 0–0.25%, large-scale Treasury/MBS purchases, expanded repos, discount window rate cut, and global swap lines) helps stabilize market functioning and supports credit availability. However, Beige Book anecdotes from this period indicate a swift, broad-based deterioration: activity shifted from modest growth pre-COVID to sharp contraction across most Districts; consumer spending, tourism, transportation, and manufacturing fell abruptly; firms reported steep layoffs; and uncertainty rose markedly. On credit, District contacts noted tightening standards and other terms across C&I and CRE, declining collateral values, rising delinquency risks, and reduced risk tolerance—corroborating the April 2020 SLOOS signal of a rapidly tightening credit channel. These real-economy and credit-supply headwinds outweigh the positive impulse from policy support near term, worsening the outlook relative to an FSR-only read.

Net effect: bias more negative than the prior SLOOS-adjusted view. Revised sentiment leans further downbeat.
